name: intent-synonyms
description:
Phrase synonyms of one intent: every variation of the phrase by the thesaurus, scored by meaning against it.

Parameters, set with --set NAME=VALUE:
- threshold (default 0): the similarity from 0 to 1 a variation needs to stay: 0 keeps every variation, 0.85 drops the ones below.
- model (default bge-m3): the encoder that scores each variation against the phrase, pulled once with `semkit models pull NAME`.
- source (default ruwordnet): the word data the synonyms come from: ruwordnet, navec or both.

Steps, as read takes them:
- synonym-candidates --all --source {source} --as-slots
- linear-combinations
- agree
- nearest --to {text} --threshold {threshold} --model {model}
- use-column match
- drop-cells empty
- sort-rows --by similarity --desc

The chain runs once for each phrase of the input, {text} being that phrase; the parts are joined in the order of the input under a first column input. An option of a step is set with --set STEP.OPTION=VALUE: it replaces the value of the option in that step, or adds the option.

Example: semkit run intent-synonyms core.csv write out.csv

options.name: --text
options.description: A phrase from the command line, repeatable, as read takes it. IN is then left out.

options.name: --set
options.description: A value of a parameter of the workflow (NAME=VALUE), or of an option of one of its steps (STEP.OPTION=VALUE); repeatable.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Read and run every step, print the summary, write nothing.

arguments.name: [IN] [write OUT]
arguments.description: The table to read, as read takes it ('-' for JSONL on stdin; left out with --text), then 'write OUT': the file to write, '-' for JSONL on stdout.
